groups.title: Strategy
groups.question: Your team's tests break every time someone refactors, but real bugs still reach production. Explain how you would decide what to test and where to start.

followUps.What to test: Why are tests that check implementation details a problem?
followUps.Unit tests with Vitest: Which code is easiest and most valuable to unit test, and why use Vitest?

evidence.text: Tests should check behavior users rely on, not how the code is written inside.
Tests tied to internals break on refactors even when nothing visible changed.
Such tests cost more to maintain than the bugs they catch.
Pure functions like reducers, formatters and validators are easy and valuable to test.
Vitest runs fast and reuses the project's Vite setup.
Its API is compatible with Jest, so existing knowledge carries over.

groups.title: Components
groups.question: You are testing a login form component that shows an error after a failed request. Explain how you would find elements and simulate the user in the test.

followUps.Queries by role: Why find a button by its role and name instead of a CSS class or test id?
followUps.User events and async UI: How do you test UI that updates after a request finishes?

evidence.text: Role and name are how users and screen readers identify elements.
These queries survive changes to class names and markup structure.
If a test cannot find an element by role, it often means the element is not accessible.
user-event simulates real typing and clicking, including focus and keyboard events.
findBy queries and waitFor wait for the UI to update after a promise resolves.
Waiting for the expected result is more reliable than waiting a fixed time.

notEnough: Only saying you would use await.

groups.title: Network
groups.question: Your components call a real API, so tests are slow and fail when the API is down, and nobody has ever seen the error screen in a test. Explain how you would test network behavior.

followUps.Mock Service Worker: How does Mock Service Worker differ from mocking fetch directly?
followUps.Testing loading and error states: How would you test that the error and empty states actually work?

evidence.text: MSW intercepts requests at the network level.
Components run their real fetching code and only the response is fake.
The same handlers can be used in tests and during development.
Special handlers can delay, fail or return empty data for a single test.
This checks states users rarely see but notice when they break.
Tests check that the right message and retry option appear in each case.

notEnough: Only saying you would test errors.

groups.title: End to End
groups.question: Your team adds end-to-end tests for checkout, but they fail randomly in CI and people have started ignoring red builds. Explain how you would set up reliable end-to-end tests.

followUps.Playwright: What does Playwright do to make end-to-end tests less flaky and easier to debug?
followUps.CI and flaky tests: Why is a flaky test dangerous, and what would you do about one?

evidence.text: Playwright drives real browsers such as Chromium, Firefox and WebKit.
It waits automatically for elements to be ready before acting.
It records traces of failed runs so you can see exactly what happened.

notEnough: Only saying Playwright runs tests in a browser.

evidence.text: Tests should run in CI on every push.
A flaky test teaches people to ignore failures, so real ones slip through.
Flaky tests should be fixed or removed quickly, and fixed sleeps replaced with waiting for real conditions.

notEnough: Only saying to rerun failed tests.
